plan.contextChunk: This figure is a single-trace ultraviolet absorption spectrum of 1,3-butadiene plotted over a pink gradient field. The vertical axis is labeled "Absorbance", carries a magenta arrow pointing up beside the label, and runs from 0 to 1.0 with labeled ticks every 0.2. The horizontal axis reads "Wavelength (nm)", is followed by a magenta arrow pointing right, and spans 200 to 400 with labeled ticks every 20 nm. One magenta curve enters at the left edge near 0.34, climbs steeply to a rounded maximum just under 0.9 at about 215 nm, then falls sharply through 240 nm to roughly 0.07, after which it declines almost imperceptibly along a near-horizontal tail to about 0.03 at the right edge. A short annotation just above and right of the crest reads "lambda max = 217 nm". With the zero baseline at the bottom of the chart rather than the top, absorption registers as a peak rising off a flat floor, and the eye is meant to fix on that lone crest against the featureless tail beyond 250 nm. The trace records the wavelength of strongest absorption for a simple conjugated diene, the reading from which molar absorptivity is calculated.

interactionPlan.concept: The UV absorption spectrum of a conjugated diene like 1,3-butadiene is dominated by a single sharp peak at lambda_max (217 nm), with negligible absorbance across the long-wavelength tail, so lambda_max marks the wavelength of strongest absorption.

interactions.label: Wavelength (nm)
interactions.teaches: Scrubbing the wavelength moves a dot along the curve and updates the absorbance readout, revealing that absorbance climbs to its single highest value at 217 nm (lambda_max) and is nearly zero everywhere in the long-wavelength tail

interactions.label: Emphasize region
interactions.teaches: Comparing the highlighted 200-250 nm crest against the highlighted >250 nm flat tail shows that essentially all of 1,3-butadiene's diagnostic UV absorption is concentrated in the narrow short-wavelength peak, not spread across the spectrum

demo_steps.title: Read the spectrum
demo_steps.narration: The magenta trace shows one sharp crest near 217 nm and a long, nearly flat tail beyond 250 nm; the annotation marks this crest as lambda_max, the wavelength of maximum absorbance.

demo_steps.title: Scub away from the peak
demo_steps.narration: Drag the wavelength slider into the tail (e.g. 300 nm): the marker dot drops to the floor and the absorbance readout falls to near zero, showing how little light is absorbed far from lambda_max.

demo_steps.title: Peak versus tail
demo_steps.narration: Toggle to 'Highlight tail' to shade the flat >250 nm region, then back to 'Highlight peak': the contrast makes clear that the diene's entire diagnostic absorption lives in the narrow short-wavelength maximum.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: lambda_max is simply the wavelength where the absorbance curve reaches its single highest point, and for a simple conjugated diene that diagnostic absorption is confined to one sharp short-wavelength peak with a featureless tail elsewhere.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Render as a Chart.js line plot on a soft pink top-to-bottom gradient background. X-axis 200-400 nm, ticks every 20; y-axis 0-1.0, ticks every 0.2; both axis labels in black with a small magenta arrow glyph (up beside 'Absorbance', right after 'Wavelength (nm)'). The single data series is a vivid magenta (~#d6006e) smooth curve: ~0.34 at 200 nm, peak ~0.87 at 217 nm, ~0.07 at 240 nm, then a gently decaying near-horizontal tail to ~0.03 at 400 nm. Place the text 'lambda_max = 217 nm' just above-right of the crest. The slider drives a filled marker dot constrained to the curve plus a small live readout label 'A = 0.xx' near the dot. For the toggle, 'Highlight peak' shades/brightens the 200-250 nm band and dims the tail; 'Highlight tail' does the reverse, shading >250 nm and dimming the crest, so the eye compares concentrated peak versus flat tail.

authoredContext:
Note that UV spectra differ from IR spectra in how they are presented. For historical reasons, IR spectra are usually displayed so that the baseline corresponding to zero absorption runs across the top of the chart and a valley indicates an absorption, whereas UV spectra are displayed with the baseline at the bottom of the chart so that a peak indicates an absorption (the figure).

The ultraviolet spectrum of 1,3-butadiene, λmax = 217 nm.

The ultraviolet spectrum of 1,3-butadiene shows a peak at (217, 0.85) where lambda max equals 217 nanometers. The x-axis and y-axis represent wavelength and absorbance, respectively.
